payload.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-17 against live psychiatry.tools (read-only HTTP, no provider access): this row's mechanism now has numbers. GET /api/search/universal?q=lithium returns Server-Timing 'documents;dur=751, medications;dur=530, services;dur=530, forms;dur=530, dsm;dur=530, differentials;dur=491, presentations;dur=437, specifiers;dur=432, formulation;dur=431, therapies;dur=431, dictionary;dur=395, tools;dur=394, total;dur=751'. The five catalogue kinds landing on the SAME ~530 ms, in parallel, is the signature this row predicts: each domain pays the whole-release scan rather than its own kind's cost, so the durations converge on the scan rather than spreading by catalogue size. Total search wall time is gated by the documents leg at 751 ms, with every catalogue leg inside it. Application-side CPU is NOT the bottleneck and is now smaller: catalogue ranking for a real query measured 21.8 ms before and 18.5 ms after the query-tokenisation fix on branch claude/psychsift-latency-review-lg2eko, i.e. roughly 3 percent of one 530 ms leg. That branch does not touch this SQL. First-call figures were 2.35 s total / 1448 ms medications, so a cold container roughly triples it. STILL OPEN and the gate is unchanged: the fix is a stored indexed kind column shipped as a migration inside an approved window, and Step 3 of scripts/operator-explain-site-content-public-records.sql must settle the push-down question first. RAISED P2->P1 ON 2026-09-20: this defect is now continuously degrading the live site, which the row did not state. Measured from public CI history only (no provider access, no live probe): live-domain-monitor failed 16 of its last 17 scheduled runs since 2026-09-16T18:34Z, the single green run being 2026-09-19T12:36Z. Every failure is the same probe and the same three lines - 'forms/services/medications: answering from the in-bundle catalogue because the published one could not be read' (run 35511141016, job 106079146903, 2026-09-20T12:37Z). Every OTHER probe passes in every one of those runs: root shell, /api/health live mode, key routes, www/TLS, deployment freshness. So the site is UP and serving current code; what is broken is that Forms, Services and Medications search answers from the in-bundle seed catalogue instead of the published one. LIKELY MECHANISM, INFERRED NOT MEASURED: catalogueSeedFallbackBudgetMs (src/lib/site-content/catalogue-seed-fallback.ts) is 1200 ms, and the post-fix latencies ledger #GCB0DV records from the 2026-09-17T18:36 run are forms 1132 ms and medications 1217 ms - straddling the budget. A read sitting on the line loses most of the time and occasionally wins, which is exactly the 16-of-17 pattern. Consistent with the evidence, but not a direct measurement; confirming it needs a live timing read, which is provider-backed and needs owner approval. COMPOUNDING: catalogueSeedFallbackCooldownMs is 30000, so one missed read sends every search to seeds for the next 30 s without retrying. WHAT IS NOT BROKEN, and it matters: the degradation is honest. catalogueDegraded threads through forms-search-results-page, services-navigator-page, medication-prescribing-workspace, differentials-home and universal-search-also-matches, and the reader sees the shared catalogueDegradedNotice 'may be out of date' beside the results heading. Nobody is shown a stale list presented as current. DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY RAISING THE BUDGET: that makes every reader wait longer and hides the condition from the monitor rather than repairing it. The fix remains this row's stored indexed kind column, which is a migration and needs an approved merge window. OFTEN CONFLATED WITH THIS, AND SEPARATE: #HTZPQ8 is that the curated records were never published into the database at all, so a fast read would still not show them.
